registered_note: This file is fixed before the first q2 run. The repository commit that adds it is the registration time. Approved by Terry J Carter 2026-10-28 11:57 CT. The wording of a prompt_2 is never edited after the start date; a change is a new series file (e1-q2-02) with its own start date.
question: When the wording of the daily question changes, does an engine still name the same businesses for a market cut? In plain terms: does being named hold up under a second, differently worded buyer question?
what_prompt_2_is: A second daily question for each row listed below: same market and niche as the row's prompt_1, a different buyer phrasing, neutral, no brand names, asks for specific businesses. It is asked of every configured answer engine (perplexity, gemini, anthropic, openai) once per day, after the whole prompt_1 pass. prompt_1 is not changed in any way.
wording_frame: I need [service or situation] in [CITY]. Which specific [company type] should I call, and why?  One frame for all ten rows; only the situation and company type change.
start_rule: The first scheduled collector run after the pull request that adds this file is merged to main. Fill start_date with that run's date_utc in a later commit; rows are dated by the collector, not by this field.
stop_rule: None before the first comparison is published. The series stops when Terry J Carter says so or when roster/e1_q2.json is replaced by a new version.

output.never_merged: q2 rows are a separate series. They are never merged into a prompt_1 count, never added to a prompt_1 denominator, and never enter Edition 1, a market cut, a public_numbers_check figure, the verify page, an evidence file or the daily datasets. Those read corpus/e1/ and NB-CZ-API_ files only; the q2 folder and prefix are chosen so that none of them can match.
output.same_extraction: Names are extracted from a q2 answer by the same code path as a prompt_1 answer (scripts/e1_runner.py extract_competitors, same gazetteer read from the prompt_1 record). A q2 answer never feeds that gazetteer.

engine_notes.openai: QUOTA_BLOCKED since 2026-10-26 (API balance). q2 rows for openai are written as QUOTA_BLOCKED like the prompt_1 rows and excluded from every denominator. If credits return they count from that day.
engine_notes.gemini: Free tier. q2 ids are never on the 20-question gemini-3.6-flash continuity panel, so a q2 Gemini call always uses gemini-3.5-flash-lite (500 requests a day). Three of the ten rows (atlanta-hvac, houston-hvac, los-angeles-ca-ai-marketing-agency) are on that panel, so their prompt_1 Gemini rows use gemini-3.6-flash and a q1 versus q2 difference there mixes wording with model. Those three are reported separately and are not part of the Gemini headline; the Gemini headline uses the seven rows whose prompt_1 and prompt_2 are both answered by gemini-3.5-flash-lite (engine_meta.requested_model records the model per row). If Gemini refuses a prompt_1 call for quota or billing earlier in the same run, the q2 Gemini cells for that day are not asked and are logged as QUOTA_BLOCKED.
engine_notes.perplexity_anthropic: Same model setting as the prompt_1 calls (scripts/engines.py). The model id each provider reports is logged per row in engine_meta.

planned_comparison.unit: One cell is one row x one engine x one day (date_utc).
planned_comparison.pairing: A cell is paired when the same row, engine and day has an OK prompt_1 row and an OK prompt_2 row. Only the first OK file of the day for each (the base file, not an _rN rerun) is used; reruns are reported separately. Unpaired cells are counted and shown, never imputed.
planned_comparison.named: For the nine research-segment rows, a business is named in an answer when it is in competitors_mentioned after the same entity gate that builds the corresponding market cut. For the Los Angeles AI marketing agency row, named is business_mentioned for Atrix Digital and, for other agencies, the same gate on competitors_mentioned.
primary_measures: 1. Hold rate, per engine and per day: of the businesses named under prompt_1 in paired cells, the share also named under prompt_2 on the same day by the same engine. Reported as k of n with n = the number of (business, row) pairs named under prompt_1.
2. Reverse hold rate, same layout: of the businesses named under prompt_2, the share also named under prompt_1.
3. Named-count comparison, per engine and per day: distinct businesses named under prompt_1 versus prompt_2, with the number of paired cells behind each figure.
4. For a business the record already counts as named under prompt_1 on a given day: whether it is named under prompt_2 on that day, shown per row, engine and day.
planned_comparison.denominators: Every figure prints its denominator: paired cells, OK rows per variant, QUOTA_BLOCKED rows, FAILED rows and rows not asked, per engine and per day. QUOTA_BLOCKED and FAILED rows are never counted as not named.
planned_comparison.aggregation: Per day and per engine first, then a pooled figure per engine over all days with the day count. No pooled figure across engines. Gemini is split into the seven same-model rows (headline) and the three panel rows (descriptive).
planned_comparison.not_claimed: No claim that prompt_2 is a better or truer question than prompt_1. No claim about which businesses are best. A low hold rate says the naming is sensitive to wording for that engine and market on those days; it does not say which wording is right.
planned_comparison.first_publication: Not before 14 paired days per engine, and never before Terry J Carter approves the text. Until then the series is collected and not cited.

disclosures.cost: Up to 40 extra calls a day (10 rows x 4 engines); 30 are billable while openai is blocked.
disclosures.kill_switch: Repository variable E1_DISABLE_Q2 = 1 stops the q2 pass on the next run; no row is deleted.
